problem: Social navigation research is evaluated on diverse robots, scenarios and environments, so algorithms are hard to compare. Existing high-fidelity simulators rarely include dynamic pedestrians, and crowd simulators are usually separate from robot simulators.
motivation: Simulation is useful across the robotics development cycle and for safety verification, but reproducible benchmarking of social navigation is limited by the effort of building systems. A high-visual-fidelity simulator with animated humans and a standardized evaluation toolkit would allow fairer comparison.
key_idea: SEAN is an open-source Unity + ROS simulation platform with animated pedestrians, ready-made scenes and robots, and a Trial Runner that repeats navigation episodes and logs social navigation metrics.
insight: The sample results show the toolkit exposes differences between controllers. The minimally tuned ROS Navigation Stack completed only 60% (Lab) and 29% (City) of episodes with the Jackal, versus 88% and 80% for teleoperation, and it had more pedestrian collisions in the city. Logging initial conditions lets episodes be replayed for fair comparison. These are only illustrative results, not an ablation.
method: Platform architecture: Unity 3D game engine (PhysX physics) connected to ROS via ROS#, so existing ROS navigation stacks can be used; runs on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 18.04 with ROS Melodic.

Scenes: two ready scenes, a lab and an outdoor city. Pedestrian start and goal positions come from crowd flow prediction plus Unity's built-in path planning, and pedestrian count and density are parameterized and repeatable.
Robots and sensors: Clearpath Jackal and Warthog models equipped with a simulated Velodyne VLP-16 LIDAR and an RGB camera.

Trial Runner: automatically runs a trial as a collection of point-to-point episodes. It configures scene, actors and robot, assigns goals, records the initial conditions for replay, and ends an episode on reaching the goal or timing out.
Metrics logging: goal reached, elapsed time, collisions with static objects, final distance to goal, closest distance to pedestrians, and number of pedestrian collisions.
Baselines: ROS Navigation Stack (minimally tuned, SLAM localization) and gamepad teleoperation, which also serves as a way to collect demonstrations.

setting.backbone: ROS Navigation Stack (classical, minimally tuned) with SLAM localization; human teleoperation baseline
setting.training_data: none (simulation platform; baselines are not learned)
setting.observation: simulated Velodyne VLP-16 LIDAR + RGB camera
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands via ROS navigation goal (point-to-point) or gamepad teleoperation

numbers_note: Only illustrative platform results (Table 1: Jackal/Warthog, Lab/City, 10 episodes, custom metrics) that do not map to a canonical benchmark, so none are listed.
results: SEAN is demonstrated in two scenes with two robots. The minimally tuned ROS Nav Stack gets 60% completion (Lab) and 29% (City) on the Jackal, while teleoperation gets 88% and 80%. The Warthog teleoperated in the city completed 100% with no collisions.
limitations: Only two scenes, two robots and a small set of metrics; the results are just 10-episode samples with a minimally tuned baseline.
Sim-to-real transfer and human evaluation of robot behavior are not yet tested.
Pedestrians follow standard pedestrian models and no learned social navigation methods are evaluated.
